title: Workload Probe Synthesis and Benchmark Suite
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines the Redwood Probe Suite: a systematic approach for synthesizing realistic workload probes and a controlled benchmarking suite used during model onboarding, quantization evaluation, and regression triage. The goal is to create reproducible, diverse probes that reflect customer-facing workloads while enabling fast, deterministic checks in CI, shadow canaries, and offline long-tail scans.

Motivation

- Many quality regressions surface only under specific workload distributions (long context, heavy system prompts, adversarial inputs, multilingual code-mixed queries).
- Existing prompt catalogs emphasize breadth but lack a compact, reproducible set of probes that exercise interaction between inference runtime (KV cache behavior, batching) and model numeric stability (quantization, attention kernels).
- We need a single, extensible artifact to: (1) seed eval harness runs, (2) act as canary probes in private/dedicated deployments, and (3) power regression triage quick-checks.

Scope

This doc covers:
1) Probe generation methodology and metadata schema.
2) Workload synthesis templates and seeding strategy.
3) Benchmark execution protocol and performance/quality metrics.
4) Integration points with the eval harness, CI, and shadow deployments.
5) Quantization-aware test variants and failure modes.
6) Operational runbook for triage and escalation.

Probe Suite Design Principles

- Deterministic by default: every probe includes a seed and execution parameters to enable bitwise reproducibility where possible.
- Hierarchical coverage: probes are grouped into micro, macro, and adversarial tiers to prioritize quick checks vs. deep dives.
- Label-rich metadata: each probe carries labels for slice (e.g., long-context, system-prompt, code, translation), target feature (e.g., streaming, tool-call), expected behavior, and risk level.
- Execution-aware: probes include runtime hints (preferred batch sizes, KV-cache warm-up pattern, recommended runtime kernel profile) so the eval harness can emulate production behavior.

Probe Metadata Schema (single-line JSON example)

{"probe_id":"rdw-p-2026-001","seed":"82439","slice_labels":["long-context","system-prompt","multilingual"],"exec_tiers":["micro","shadow_canary"],"expected_assertions":["no-truncation","response-stability-index > 0.95"],"runtime_hints":{"warmup_prefix":"<SYS>Remember user prefs</SYS>","batch_hint":"auto:8"}}

Note: the actual stored probe objects in the probe registry use the above flat schema fields (the eval harness will accept this set of keys).

Workload Synthesis Patterns

A. Temporal Composition (conversation-laden probes)\- Simulate repeated turns with incremental context growth to exercise KV-cache and attention scaling.
- Template: 6-turn dialog, each turn ~150–400 tokens, include intermittent system instructions.
- Use-case: chat streaming latency, KV cache eviction heuristics.

B. Prefix-heavy System Prompts\- Very long system context preceding short user query. Tests prefix-cutting, streaming flush behavior, and tokenization boundary effects.

C. Functional Code + Natural Language Mix\- Small code snippets embedded in text; test tokenization and generation consistency after quantized kernels.

D. Multilingual / Code-mixed Inputs\- 50/50 language mix (e.g., English + Simplified Chinese) to probe tokenization edge cases, embedding drift, and translation regressions.

E. Adversarial Perturbations\- Typos, Unicode homoglyphs, punctuation storms to exercise robustness layers and guardrails.

Seeding Strategy and Probe Families

- Seed pools: each probe references a random seed from one of three pools (core, longtail, adversarial). Seeds are recorded in the probe manifest and are stable.
- Probe families: group probes by primary axis (latency sensitivity, accuracy sensitivity, hallucination risk). Examples:
  - Core conversational family (fast CI checks)
  - Deep-context family (nightly long runs)
  - Quant-sensitivity family (used before/after quantization)

Benchmark Execution Protocol

1) Triage Phase (micro checks)
  - Run time: < 5 minutes.
  - Probes: core conversational family, 12 items.
  - Metrics collected: P95 latency, token-throughput, Rerank-match-rate (if applicable), basic QA exact match.

2) Canary Phase (shadow canaries)
  - Run time: continuous / rolling.
  - Probes: selected shadow_canary tier probes, executed against 1% of traffic in sandboxed routing.
  - Metrics: same as triage plus streaming-completeness and partial-response-availability.

3) Deep Validation (quant/regression suites)
  - Run time: nightly / pre-promotion.
  - Probes: full quant-sensitivity + deep-context families (~800 probes).
  - Metrics: Response Stability Index (RSI), semantic-similarity A/B vs baseline, hallucination score, calibration drift, per-slice token-efficiency.

Metric Definitions (short)

- Response Stability Index (RSI): fraction of runs (n=5) where normalized semantic similarity (ROUGE/BERTScore/embedding cosine) >= threshold. Represented as 0.0–1.0.
- Latency SLOs: P95 < 1200ms for hosted small-context probes; P95 < 2500ms for long-context probes.
- Token Efficiency: effective tokens per user intent (derived from reference length).

Integration with Eval Harness

- Probe manifest format: newline-delimited JSONL. Each line is a flat JSON object matching the metadata schema above.
- Invocation: eval-harness CLI supports --probe-manifest and --runtime-profile flags. Example:
  rdw-eval-run --probe-manifest probes/core.manifest.jsonl --runtime-profile g5-16x --repeats 3 --output results/core-vs-baseline.jsonl

- Runtime profiles map to kernel selection and batch parameters. Profiles are versioned in the eval harness and included in CI snapshots.

Quantization-aware Considerations

- For quant-sensitivity family, include paired probes: float32 baseline and target quant step. Each pair uses identical seeds and execution order; only model binary changes.
- Recommended probe subset for quick quant check: 120 probes span (long-context, code-mix, system-prefix).
- Failure modes to watch for post-quant: sudden RSI drop, increased repetition, off-by-one tokenization errors, or elevated hallucination score on safety probes.

Quality Gate Thresholds (example)

| Gate | Micro | Canary | Promotion requirement |
|------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| RSI (core) | >= 0.95 | >= 0.93 | >= 0.94 (vs last prod) |
| Hallucination (safety slice) | <= 0.02 | <= 0.03 | <= 0.03 |
| P95 latency | <= 1200ms | <= 1500ms | no regression > +10% |

Note: Use sliding baseline windows (14-day) for promotion decisions.

Regression Triage Hooks

When a post-promotion regression is detected, follow this quick triage path:
1) Reproduce: run the failing probe pair locally with identical runtime profile and repeats=5.
2) Isolate: toggle variables in this order: model version, quantization flag, runtime-profile (kernel), batch-size, KV-cache behavior.
3) Log & Snapshot: collect full trace, attention-map dump, token-level logits for failing probe seeds. Store in shared triage bucket: s3://redwood-evals/triage/<incident-id>/
4) Bisect: if not isolated, start binary rollbacks over model commits or quantizer commits using the automated regression-bisect tool.
5) Mitigate: if regression impacts production SLOs, trigger automated fallback routing to baseline model variant and open an oncall incident.

Operational Runbook (play-by-play)

- Nightly job: run deep validation suite, publish results to /dashboards/eval/suites/deep-validation.
- Pre-promotion gate: must pass micro + quant quick-check with no quality gates violated.
- Post-deploy monitoring: enable shadow_canary probes at 1% traffic for 72 hours.
- Incident play: if RSI delta > 0.07 for core family, open incident, notify ML-SRE and Applied-ML.

Example Probe YAML (compact)

- probe_id: rdw-p-2026-257
  seed: 66281
  title: "Help me refactor a SQL query with 3 joins (long context)"
  slice_labels: ["long-context","sql","performance"]
  exec_tiers: ["deep","pre-promotion"]
  expected_assertions: ["no-truncation","contains-optimized-query"]
  runtime_profile: g5-16x-quant-check

Best Practices and Maintenance

- Review and rotate seed pools quarterly to avoid overfitting to synthetic artifacts.
- Curate a small fast-core (<= 30 probes) for CI that covers all critical slices.
- Version probe manifests alongside model promotions. Do not mutate probes in-place; always create new manifest versions.

FAQ

Q: Can product teams add domain-specific probes?
A: Yes — submit probes to the probe-registry repo with required metadata and label assignment; maintainers will review for conflicts and redundancy.

Q: How to keep probe suite small but effective?
A: Use hierarchical tiers, rely on representative seeds, and focus on slices that historically produce regressions (long context, code-mix, heavy system prompts).

Appendix A: Triaging Checklist (quick)

1) Reproduce with identical seed and runtime profile.
2) Compare logits and embeddings vs baseline.
3) Swap model binary -> does issue persist?
4) Swap quantizer -> if resolves, escalate to quant infra owner.
5) Run targeted unit tests for tokenization and streaming flush.
6) Document root cause and remedial rollout plan.
